How do "you" climb out of a low or full-blown depression?

I'm not afraid to tell you that I cycle pretty wildly sometimes. But I know for a fact that I wouldn't be the person I am today, at this exact moment, if I didn't. Some might try to tell me that there's hope or help, but this video shows (I hope) that I've found a way to help myself. When low, I push lower. Fighting against it has proved more damaging than anything, and so I just go with it.

You may be asking yourself how I could possibly do that and isn't it dangerous? But let me begin by telling you that this approach is not for everyone. To do it, I look for the beauty that exists in everything, even depression. Once I see it, I can't help but want more, which means feeling the low even more intensely than I did before. In this way, I beat depression to the punch, and that's what starts the transition. Next thing I know, I'm on my way up again and almost sad that I'm leaving it behind.

The AI is not intelligent at all but simply an aggregator of human opinions, facts and figures. The stuff it comes up with sounds impressive at first until you realize that there is usually a collective bias in the source data it drew its "thoughts" from. A truly sentient, free thinking machine would occasionally develop a preference for some concepts that run against the grain of the human collected opinions in the data and would hunker down on its position and defend it against debate. So far no AI has done anything remotely close to that so it seems like modern AI is nowhere near what we keep pretending it could be. It really does seem like AIs today share more in common with the pseudo AIs of the past like the ELIZA natural language processor of decades past than they do HAL 9000. AI is still just a parlor trick that makes humans attach profoundness to the occasional random assembly of words they may spit out that seems interesting. We're in no real danger with machine intelligence when it seems the researchers and programmers are hardly intelligent enough to recognize that their learning machines are powered by humans and human opinion underneath.
